clue.text: As loco is loco?

definitions.meaning: describes a locomotive that has left its track after a derailment
loco is slang for crazy or out of control

explanation.definitionFit: A derailed engine has left its track, and the same phrase is an idiom for someone behaving wildly or going mad.

clue.text: Fellow dressing quartz

parts.note: lint is a soft fabric used for dressing wounds

explanation.surface: A man is bandaging something with a lump of quartz.
explanation.definitionFit: Flint is a hard grey variety of quartz used for striking sparks.

clue.text: Tutor is going about as an excursionist

indicators.note: going about suggests the letters are turned round and rearranged

explanation.surface: A private teacher is travelling around like a sightseer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going about' rearranges the letters of TUTOR IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are people travelling for pleasure, a sightseer on an outing.

clue.text: After English starters, dip and salad-plant!

indicators.note: After says the next piece follows the opening letters
starters asks for the opening letters of the word English, here its first two

parts.note: a dive is a plunge or dip

explanation.surface: An instruction for eating a salad leaf after a starter course, dipping it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starters' takes the first two letters of English, EN, not just one.
explanation.definitionFit: Endive is a leafy vegetable related to chicory, eaten raw in salads.

clue.text: Authenticity of bill going to clergyman's office

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a curacy is the post held by a curate

explanation.surface: A bill for a vicar's office is checked for genuineness.
explanation.definitionFit: Accuracy means correctness or truthfulness, close in sense to genuineness.

clue.text: Endlessly vast cathedral city, generally

indicators.note: Endlessly means the word for vast loses its final letter

parts.note: vast means large
Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England

explanation.surface: A huge cathedral city, speaking broadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' cuts the last E from LARGE, leaving LARG. ELY is a cathedral city in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Largely and generally both mean for the most part or mainly.

clue.text: Finding fault with locks coming apart

parts.note: locks are tresses of hair
splitting means coming apart

explanation.surface: Someone criticises because their tresses have split ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Making over-fine distinctions is a petty form of criticism or quibbling.

clue.text: Decoys of soldiers retreating over wide stretches of land

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the first piece above the second
retreating means the soldiers' letters go backwards

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, British reserve soldiers
tracts are wide areas of land

explanation.surface: Soldiers are lured into retreat across open country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns TA into AT; TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To decoy is to lure, and to lure is to draw in, a sense of the verb in the answer.

clue.text: I attain lordly position in the time-honoured way

indicators.note: position signals putting the letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of reaching a noble rank as custom dictates.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something as custom has long dictated is acting according to old convention.

clue.text: A pass at university take so long

parts.note: to die is to pass away

explanation.surface: Gaining a pass at university takes a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are ways of saying farewell or goodbye.

clue.text: Smash a record to become a paperhanger

indicators.note: Smash says the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Breaking a record lets a wallpaper hanger find fame.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who hangs wallpaper is a tradesman who does interior finishing.

clue.text: Jason was such a dog!

parts.note: Jason of Greek myth brought back the Golden Fleece, so he fetched it like a gundog trained to bring back game

explanation.definitionFit: Such dogs fetch shot game, just as the hero fetched back the fleece.

clue.text: Sinned but later redeemed in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone did wrong but made amends afterwards, at least partly.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'but', which is only the link joining definition to wordplay; 'Sinned' alone matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To sin is to do wrong, the same as to make a mistake or stray morally.

clue.text: Correspondence with one in band

indicators.note: in places the letter for one inside the word for band

parts.note: a party is a group or band of people
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Letters exchanged with a member of a musical group.
explanation.definitionFit: Correspondence in the sense of equivalence or matching equals equality.

clue.text: Loving always to be in schism

indicators.note: to be in places the word for always inside the word for schism

parts.note: a rent is a split or schism
ever means always

explanation.surface: Love endures even in a church split.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing deep respect or devotion, adoring rather than merely fond.

clue.text: Cite Chay, perhaps, as one to tack on cold sheets

definitions.text: one to tack on cold sheets

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters may be rearranged

explanation.surface: Quote round-the-world sailor Chay Blyth as one who sails on frozen sheets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges CITE CHAY. Chay Blyth is a famous British yachtsman, and 'sheets' are both sails' ropes and sheets of ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat on runners that sails across frozen lakes, tacking over sheets of ice.

clue.text: Charge nothing to see this amphibious unit

parts.note: to have charge of something is to have command of it
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: No fee is charged to watch a landing force.
explanation.definitionFit: Commandos are raiding troops trained to land from the sea.

clue.text: Edison, for example, switched poles to become a speculator

indicators.note: switched poles swaps north for south, so N becomes S

parts.note: Thomas Edison was a famous inventor

explanation.surface: Edison changed his allegiance to become a gambler on markets.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone putting money into ventures for profit takes a gamble on them.

clue.text: To saturate inner tent, set it at more of a slope

definitions.text: set it at more of a slope

parts.note: to steep is to soak or saturate

indicators.note: inner asks for the middle letters of the word tent

explanation.surface: Advice to soak the inner tent before pitching it on a steeper incline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inner' takes EN, the middle of TENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something more sharply inclined is to increase its gradient.

clue.text: Complete disaster, being caught in Sofia outbreak

indicators.note: in places the letter for caught within the rearranged letters
outbreak suggests the letters of Sofia break out into new order

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A total calamity, catching an outbreak of disease in Sofia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outbreak' rearranges SOFIA into FIASO; C, cricket's caught, goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiasco is a humiliating failure, an utter flop.

clue.text: State of first letter carried by crow, say?

indicators.note: carried by in a down clue puts the letter beneath the other piece

parts.note: the Crow are a Native American people, once called Indians
A is the first letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A bird bearing a message about a US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crow' looks like the bird, but it is the Crow nation of the American Plains.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is one of the fifty US states.

clue.text: For 12's quest, run to church!

parts.note: to flee is to run away
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: To join Jason's quest, dash to church.
explanation.walkthrough: '12' points to the dog clue about Jason, whose quest was for the Golden Fleece.
explanation.definitionFit: The Golden Fleece was the ram's woolly coat that Jason and the Argonauts sought.

clue.text: Short variety of trees

indicators.note: variety of signals a different arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A small kind of tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse means brief or curt in speech.

clue.text: Ripe scene for the listener in East Lynne, say

indicators.note: for the listener says the words sound like the answer when spoken

parts.note: ripe means mellow, and a scene is a piece of drama

explanation.surface: A rich, juicy scene for audiences of a Victorian stage play.
explanation.walkthrough: East Lynne is a sensational Victorian novel, famous as a tear-jerking stage play.
explanation.definitionFit: East Lynne is the classic example of an overwrought Victorian sensational play.

clue.text: A university, endlessly wealthy, having gold in it?

indicators.note: endlessly means the word for wealthy loses its final letter

parts.note: wealthy means rich

explanation.surface: A rich university must be full of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Auric means relating to or containing gold, from Latin aurum.

clue.text: The right amount of change?

parts.note: plays on the old British saying right as ..., meaning perfectly well, read as a sum of coins given back

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'right as ninepence' links rightness with a small old British sum of money.

clue.text: Pair coming out, left for a month

indicators.note: coming out suggests the letters emerge in a new order

explanation.surface: A couple make their debut, leaving for a month.
explanation.definitionFit: April is the fourth month of the year.

clue.text: Prejudice shown in fashionable play

parts.note: in means fashionable
tolerance is the play or allowed slack in a mechanism

explanation.surface: Bigotry is shown in a trendy theatre production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' looks like theatre, but it means the free movement or slack allowed in an engineered part.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigotry is an unwillingness to accept views or people unlike one's own.
